questions.question: In a chemical reaction, what name is given to the starting chemicals that react together?
options: Catalysts
Reactants
Products
Solvents

questions.question: What are the chemicals that are newly formed as a result of a chemical reaction called?
options: Reactants
Catalysts
Products
Elements

questions.question: During a chemical reaction, what happens to the atoms present in the reactants?
options: They are destroyed and replaced by new atoms
They are rearranged and bonded differently in the products
They turn into a completely different element
They remain bonded in exactly the same way

questions.question: Which of the following describes Dalton's historical model of an atom?
options: A sphere that cannot be broken up
A positive sphere with embedded negative electrons
A dense nucleus surrounded by orbiting electrons
A cloud of empty space containing moving neutrons

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an element?
options: A substance made of two or more types of atoms chemically joined
A substance made up of only one type of atom
A mixture of different metal atoms
A compound of non-metals

questions.question: In a chemical formula, what do the small subscript numbers next to the chemical symbols represent?
options: The number of electrons in the outer shell
The number of chemical bonds
The number of each type of atom in the compound
The temperature at which the compound forms

questions.question: How can carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO2) be different compounds if they contain the same elements?
options: They contain the same elements but in a different ratio
One is an element and the other is a mixture
Carbon dioxide has different types of carbon atoms
Carbon monoxide is not chemically bonded

questions.question: What is a metalloid element?
options: An element that has only the properties of non-metals
An element that has some properties of metals and some of non-metals
A metal that is highly magnetic
A liquid non-metal

questions.question: How do the properties of a compound compare to the properties of the individual elements it is made from?
options: They are always a direct average of the elements' properties
They are identical to the properties of the metal element
They may be completely different from those of the elements
They are always intermediate between a solid and a liquid

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-metal element that is an excellent conductor of electricity and heat?
options: Sulfur
Phosphorus
Graphite
Oxygen

questions.question: Where are metals and non-metals positioned in the periodic table?
options: Metals are on the right side; non-metals are on the left side
Metals are on the left and in the middle; non-metals are on the right side
Metals are in the top half; non-metals are in the bottom half
Metals are in the bottom half; non-metals are in the top half

questions.question: What is meant when a non-metal gas like oxygen (O2) is described as forming a diatomic molecule?
options: The molecule contains two different elements
The molecule contains two atoms
The molecule cannot react with other elements
The molecule is made of two compounds

questions.question: Where in the periodic table are the noble gases found, and how do they exist?
options: In the left-hand column, as diatomic molecules
In the right-hand column, as monatomic atoms
In the middle section, as giant structures
In the bottom row, as diatomic molecules

questions.question: What does the ending '-ide' in a compound name like 'sodium chloride' indicate?
options: The compound contains oxygen atoms
A simple metal and non-metal have chemically bonded
The substance is a liquid at room temperature
The compound contains three different elements

questions.question: If a compound consists of metal atoms chemically bonded to an -SO4 group, what type of compound is it?
options: A metal carbonate
A metal nitrate
A metal sulfate
A metal oxide
